key_highlights: Iron ore crash confirmed, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX and the ASX Materials index
Houthis seize vital oil choke point; oil spike drives energy sector higher but pressures airlines and consumer costs
ASX set to open lower on Wall Street weakness; tech stocks weigh on global sentiment
Fed meeting in focus; RBA policy path uncertain amid fuel price blowout and second excise cut pressure
Australian housing market shows no spring bounce; auction volumes soft, prices under downward pressure
AI sector strength continues globally (Snowflake, Adobe, NVIDIA) but Trump's AI rhetoric adds volatility
Consumer sector stress: multiple retail/foodservice closures signal weakening discretionary spending
Mining exploration positives: Critica 19Mt tin-tungsten, Forrestania gold, Sarytogan graphite yield
Major private hospital operator breakup signals healthcare sector consolidation
Australia nears energy inflection point; Bowen's Saudi fuel supply mission underscores energy security concerns

sectors.trend: Iron ore crash is the dominant negative; however, exploration wins in tin, tungsten, gold, and battery-grade graphite provide selective upside. China's pivot toward Trump regime change adds geopolitical uncertainty to commodity demand.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face near-term downside on iron ore. Small/mid-cap explorers (Critica, Forrestania, Sarytogan, PLC Resources) attract speculative interest. Diversified miners with copper/gold exposure relatively insulated.

sectors.trend: Houthi seizure of oil choke point triggers oil spike; Australia nears energy inflection point. Bowen's Saudi fuel mission signals government urgency. Shipping giant installing 35m sail to cut fuel costs reflects structural cost pressure.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX), and oil services names benefit from higher crude. Airlines (QAN.AX) and transport face margin compression. Energy transition stocks gain policy tailwind.

sectors.trend: Fed meeting in focus; fuel price blowout pressures RBA to hold or cut. Housing market weakness (no spring bounce, falling prices) pressures mortgage growth and NIM. Consumer stress (retail closures) raises credit risk.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate cuts and soft housing. Willis Lease Finance (WLFC) shows growth-with-shrinking-profit pattern. Healthcare M&A (hospital operator breakup) creates lending/consolidation opportunities.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator breakup after lender-backed consortium bid signals sector consolidation. Bird flu in endangered sea lion adds biosecurity risk to ag/health nexus.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, HIC.AX, IAG.AX (health insurance) in focus. Hospital operator breakup may create acquisition targets for larger operators. Biosecurity risk to agricultural supply chains.

sectors.trend: Multiple closures: national clothing chain shutting all stores, 38-year steakhouse closing 40+ locations, coffeehouse Chapter 11. Fuel price blowout squeezes household budgets. Gen Z alcohol decline noted.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX, and discretionary retail face headwinds. Defensive staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX) relatively resilient. Consumer sentiment deteriorating ahead of potential second excise cut.

sectors.trend: Global AI momentum strong (Snowflake blowout, Adobe AI revenue, NVIDIA GPU demand) but Trump's 'SICK conspiracy' rhetoric and doomsday warnings add volatility. AI agents integrating with Visa/Mastercard payments.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (WTC.AX, XRO.AX) benefit from global AI sentiment. Payments sector (WBC.AX, CBA.AX) gains from AI agent adoption. Volatility elevated on Trump policy risk.

sectors.trend: No spring bounce in auction market; house prices under downward pressure. Melbourne fringe planning failures signal supply constraints. Young homeowners welcoming falling prices.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure. Residential property developers under stress. Commercial REITs relatively insulated but rate-sensitive.

Hedge energy costs; favour upstream producers; monitor AUD/USD for import cost pass-through
Maintain cash buffers; avoid leveraged positions ahead of Fed meeting
Underweight residential REITs and property developers; favour income-generating commercial assets
Shift from discretionary to defensive staples; monitor retail sales data
Diversify tech exposure; avoid single-name concentration in AI pure-plays
Monitor labour-intensive sectors (construction, hospitality) for demand impact

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight upstream energy producers on oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Houthi choke point control and Bowen's Saudi mission signal sustained elevated crude; WDS and STO benefit directly

opportunities.recommendation: Selective mining exploration plays on WA/Tassie discoveries
opportunities.rationale: Critica 19Mt tin-tungsten, Forrestania gold, Sarytogan 97.7% graphite yield, PLC Resources gold target offer asymmetric upside
Hospital operator breakup creates M&A targets; larger operators and health insurers benefit from sector rationalisation

opportunities.recommendation: Defensive consumer staples on spending downgrade
opportunities.rationale: Retail closures and fuel blowout shift consumer spend to essentials; WOW and WES gain relative strength

defensive_moves.rationale: Confirmed iron ore crash with China demand uncertainty; BHP/RIO/FMG face 10-15% downside risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge equity beta ahead of Fed meeting
defensive_moves.rationale: Wall Street red, ASX set to slip, stock shock building; use index puts or increase cash allocation
No spring bounce, falling prices, soft auctions; rate cut cycle may not offset demand weakness
Multiple sector closures signal structural demand erosion; fuel costs amplify household budget pressure

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely opens lower on Wall Street weakness and iron ore crash. Oil spike provides energy sector support but broad market negative. Fed meeting adds two-way volatility. Expect ^AXJO to test recent lows. AUD/USD pressured by risk-off sentiment. Key watch: whether iron ore stabilises and oil spike magnitude.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Iron ore structural oversupply and China demand shift cap materials upside. Energy transition and AI adoption provide secular growth pockets. Housing correction may extend 6-9 months. RBA likely to cut 25-50bps in coming months, supporting financials and property but not offsetting commodity weakness. Immigration policy shift may constrain labour supply and productivity.
